kinds.label: Ratio and number
kinds.desc: Harmony as proportion: consonances, tuning, numbers that measure sound or the cosmos.

kinds.label: Unlike things in one whole
kinds.desc: Harmony as a joining of opposites or of different parts, each kept different.

kinds.label: Order and rank
kinds.desc: Harmony as the right ordering of a whole: the cosmos, the soul, a hierarchy.

kinds.label: Balance and temperament
kinds.desc: Harmony as a mean or a good mixture: health, temperament, evenness of mind.

kinds.label: Concord among people
kinds.desc: Harmony as agreement in a city, a church, a society or between peoples.

kinds.label: Resonance and sympathy
kinds.desc: Like answering like: strings that sound together, sympathy and antipathy, ganying 感應.

ideas.q: Is harmony a whole made of unlike parts, each kept different?

notes.Ṛgveda|||Indian: this is a counter-case. The Vedic order concept is regularity, and the Vedic concord concept is sameness of mind. It lines up with Yanzi's *tong*, not with *he*. It supports: the Veda cannot be listed as a witness for diversity in wholeness.
notes.Chāndogya Upaniṣad (the udgītha and Om)|: this is a strong disagreement. Yanzi's soup and Uddālaka's honey use the same culinary image of many flavours in one food, and draw opposite morals. In the soup, the distinctness of the ingredients is the harmony. In the honey, the loss of distinctness is the truth. A paper that says "all traditions" hold “Harmony is diversity in wholeness” must answer this text.

notes.Bhagavad Gītā|||Indian: this is a counter-case at two levels. At the level of the person, harmony-like terms mean indifference to opposites. At the level of society, they mean a fixed division of labour by birth. The Gītā does not claim that differences strengthen the whole. It tells each part to keep its place.
notes.Caraka Saṃhitā|||Indian: two different answers sit in one book. *Sāmya* is equality of measure, which “Harmony is diversity in wholeness” would class with "the mean". The tripod is mutual support among unlike parts, which is “Harmony is diversity in wholeness” proper.
notes.Bharata, Nāṭyaśāstra|||Indian: rasa supports the definition well. It is a whole that no single component produces, and it requires unlike ingredients, just like Yanzi's soup. The traditions are independent, so this is convergence and not influence. It cuts against the definition in one respect. Bharata makes the components *serve* the durable state, which "attains the status of rasa". The parts do not flourish in their own right; they are subordinated to a dominant state.
notes.Mataṅga, Bṛhaddeśī|||Indian: the jāti etymology is the best Indian music-theory support for "a whole born from unlike parts". The king–minister–enemy image is the clearest counter-evidence. The whole is a hierarchy with one ruler, and the dissonant part is excluded. Together they show the tradition holding both, and the definition should quote both.
notes.Abhinavagupta, Abhinavabhāratī|||Indian: this is the decisive test the brief asked for. The answer is that rasa is unity reached *through* diversity, then valued *above* it. That is a third position, distinct from both the soup (, where diversity is the harmony) and the honey (, where diversity is simply lost). Diversity is necessary as means, and set aside as end.
notes.Śārṅgadeva, Saṅgītaratnākara|||Indian: consonance is defined by service to the whole: the samvādī "sustains" the rāga the vādī creates. Dissonance is defined by harm to the whole: the vivādī destroys rakti. This matches the definition's line between disharmony as a misfit that detracts and dissonance that serves. It also cuts *against* the definition: here the vivādī is simply the misfit, with no room for dissonance that serves the whole.
notes.Vinaya, Mahāvagga V.1: Soṇa and the lute: this is a strong counter-example to "found in all cultures". The best-known Buddhist musical image of balance teaches the mean. It belongs with Aristotle's virtue as a mean, not with Philolaus or Yanzi's soup.
notes.Analects 1.12 and 13.23 (he er bu tong)|: cite 13.23 for "not sameness", but always with 1.12. The pair shows a tradition that rejects homogenization while placing the guard against domination nowhere. In Zhu Xi the hierarchy *is* the harmony.
notes.Guoyu, Shi Bo in the \"Zhengyu\"|||Chine: "sameness does not continue" is a direct ancient statement that homogenization is a failure of harmony. Here it is a failure of *continuance* (the line dies out), which also links it to sustainability.
notes.Zuozhuan, Yanzi on harmony and sameness: keep the soup and the single-note lute as evidence that *he* requires difference (homogenization = water with water). Do not use them as evidence that the parts must flourish. The text supports the first half of the definition and is silent on, or against, the guard clause.

notes.Zhuangzi, \"Qiwulun\" and \"Xu Wugui\"||: the piping passage is a natural image of many unlike voices sounding together, with no conductor ("should there be any other agency that excites them?"). The critique marks what is missing.
notes.Xunzi, \"Discourse on Music\" (Yuelun)||: this is a strong counter-case inside the Chinese tradition that is usually cited *for* the definition. Within a few generations of the he/tong texts, Xunzi uses *tong* positively and makes music-harmony the homogenizing pole.
notes.Lüshi chunqiu, the music chapters|||Chin: a disagreeing witness. Harmony is fit and moderation under the One, and that is a different idea of harmony, not a weak form of ours.
notes.Huainanzi|||Chinese: the Yuandao supports the guard clause. Harmony is reached while "ten thousand differences" each "find convenience in their own nature", so the parts are not sacrificed. But the passage gets there through *non-action* and having "no likes or dislikes" (Gao You's gloss), which is quietist, not a mechanism.
notes.Liji, \"Record of Music\" (Yueji)|||Chin: this is the closest classical statement of the definition's two opposites. Excess union ("weak coalescence") points toward homogenization, and excess distinction ("separation") points toward fragmentation. It also cuts *against* the definition. In the Yueji, harmony (music) is the *uniting* pole, and diversity is supplied by a different institution (ceremony). The whole is the pair, so "harmony" in this text means union, not diversity in wholeness. That is closer to *tong* than Yanzi would allow.
notes.Zhang Zai, Zhengmeng, \"Supreme Harmony\: point 3 states homogenization ("sameness that cannot differ is conformity") and fragmentation ("difference that cannot be the same disrupts order") as the two failures, in a Neo-Confucian text.
notes.Zhu Xi, on equilibrium and harmony (zhon: a disagreeing witness. Zhu Xi's most influential definition of he makes "no discord" the criterion, which is the reverse of "dissonance belongs inside".
notes.Zhu Zaiyu, Yuelü quanshu (equal temperam: he cuts *against* the diversity half. Equal temperament makes all twelve steps identical, which homogenizes the intervals for the sake of the whole (free modulation, "rotating the mode", 旋宮). Diversity moves from the intervals to the keys and modes.

notes.Kangen ongi|||Japanese: another case for the guard clause. A whole made of different parts is called harmonious when the parts submit.
notes.Zeami, Fūshikaden|||Japanese: supports the core claim that harmony needs unlikeness. It is a third, independent witness alongside the Greek and the Chinese, from a working performer rather than a cosmologist.
notes.Kaibara Ekiken, on music and harmony|||J: another case for the guard clause. A whole made of different parts is called harmonious when the parts submit.

notes.Plato, Phaedo (the soul as attunement)||: Plato supports the "fragmentation" pole: an unmeasured mixture is a "jumble" that destroys its own parts (Philebus 64e). Eight different notes make one harmony (Republic X). But he cuts AGAINST the definition in two ways. First, limit "puts an end to the differences between opposites" (Philebus 26a), so harmony resolves tension rather than keeping it. Second, his concord is hierarchical: reason is the "natural lord", and the Republic's harmony of the classes rests on each part keeping to its station. "The parts flourish" here means the parts obey, which is exactly the risk the guard clause exists to block. He names sameness as a failure only for songs: the city's strains must vary "to take away the effect of sameness" (Laws II, 665c). The variety is in the music, while the citizens sing as one; he never names homogenization of people as a failure.

A concord (*symphonia*) turned into unison (*homophonia*) is a worse whole, not a purer one. It parallels Yanzi's single zither note. Problems XIX.38 states "a mixing of opposites that have a ratio" outright. **Against the definition:** Aristotle's remedy for a city that is too unified is education, custom and law, which make the many "one" (II.5). He also defends natural rulers and slaves (Politics I). For him the parts are differentiated, but they do not all flourish.

notes.Euclid, Sectio canonis|||Greek: "a single blending of the two" is harmony as fusion of two into one. It sits nearer the homogenization pole than “Harmony is diversity in wholeness” would like. It is a perceptual claim about two tones, not a claim about wholes.
notes.Nicomachus, Manual of Harmonics|||Hellen: support at the level of number. The "most perfect" harmonia is not one ratio but three different kinds of mean held in one four-term structure. The difference between the means is what makes it harmonia.
notes.Theon of Smyrna, Mathematics Useful for: point 1 is the ancient formula closest to "diversity in wholeness": *enantiōn synarmogē* and *tōn pollōn henōsis*. But its end state is like-mindedness and good order under law.
notes.Ptolemy, Harmonics|||Hellenistic & Late: Ptolemy cuts AGAINST the definition. notes.Plotinus, Enneads (IV.4 on sympathy)|||H: III.2.17 states the definition almost word for word. The whole is not beautiful "if every thing is as a stone" (homogenization). It is beautiful when unequal parts each give "a proper tone" to "one entire harmony", and dissonance belongs inside the whole. **But it cuts against the guard clause.** This is theodicy: souls placed "in darkness, and in Tartarus" are justified because they serve the whole. The whole flourishes and the part need not. III.6.2 supplies the corrective in Plotinus's own words: each part must "sing well … as far as pertains to his own part", and each part's own virtue comes *before* the harmony.
notes.Aristides Quintilianus, On Music|||Helle: little direct bearing in the pages read. Harmony here is the corrective tuning of a soul, not a whole of unlike parts.

notes.Boethius, On the Institution of Music|||: I.3 is a direct ancestor of the definition. Identical sounds make no consonance; difference "reduced into one" does. I.8 even pictures dissonance as fragmentation: each sound "strives … to arrive as a complete whole" and obstructs the other. But I.1 cuts AGAINST the definition. Delight is like answering like, and "unlikeness is hateful", which is why each people loves the modes of its own character. Boethius therefore needs two levels: difference *between notes*, likeness *between music and listener*.

notes.Ṛgveda|||Indian: one word, ṛta, covers sky, rite and truthful speech. This is a genuine multi-level order concept. But it links the levels by a single law, not by a whole made of diverse parts at each level.

Where Descartes said beauty has no fixed measure, Euler says the order is really there and that a listener who does not hear it is mistaken.

notes.Hermann von Helmholtz, On the Sensations: the mind does not perceive ratios. It feels whether nerve excitation is continuous or intermittent. *, and it agrees with Hutcheson that knowing the cause adds nothing to the feeling.
notes.Charles Darwin, The Descent of Man (on m: Darwin gives the feeling side a mechanism. The standard is the chooser's preference ("their standard of beauty"), not a ratio. That is the partial bridge from evolution that “Feeling harmony and thinking it: the thousand-year question” mentions, with its 1859 seed now on a page.
notes.Aristotle, On the Heavens II.9 (against: the Problems give a feeling-from-number answer: we enjoy consonance because "ratio is order, which is naturally pleasant". The Politics gives a second answer that is not about number. Modes are likenesses of character that we learn to enjoy by habituation.

ideas.q: Can harmony be measured before what it is said to explain?
ideas.t: Harmony as a research programme, like natural selection and spectroscopy

notes.Caraka Saṃhitā|||Indian: Caraka makes evenness a *measurable* target ("increase or decrease the quantity" in Suśruta). That is the kind of operational definition the research programme wants. It measures balance, not diversity.
notes.Bharata, Nāṭyaśāstra|||Indian: the two-vīṇā demonstration is a reproducible procedure for measuring an interval by ear. It is a measurement before theory.
notes.Liji, \"Record of Music\" (Yueji)|||Chin: "the airs of an age … indicate" its order. This treats music as a readable *measure* of social harmony before any outcome, which is the measure-first idea of the research programme in an ancient form.
notes.Zhu Zaiyu, Yuelü quanshu (equal temperam: his move is to replace an approximation with a computed exact value, carried to 25 digits, and that is a measurement programme. Whether his pipes sounded right is a separate question that the pages do not address.
notes.Nicomachus, Manual of Harmonics|||Hellen: the "consistent and unerring" generalisation from hammers to bowls and pipes is an over-reach that is false in physics. It is a warning case of a law declared from one dramatic observation and never tested.
notes.Ptolemy, Harmonics|||Hellenistic & Late: Harmonics I.2 is a methods statement. Hypotheses must "save" what is heard, as astronomy saves the motions, and the Pythagoreans failed because their ratios clashed with the phenomena. This is the oldest model-must-fit-data rule in harmonics.
notes.al-Fārābī, Great Book of Music|||Arabic: he proposes an intersubjective, majority standard for consonance, "as in astronomy". That is a measurement protocol a thousand years early, and it has the sampling problem the Tsimane' work exposes.
notes.al-Fārābī, The Virtuous City|||Arabic: he proposes an intersubjective, majority standard for consonance, "as in astronomy". That is a measurement protocol a thousand years early, and it has the sampling problem the Tsimane' work exposes.
notes.Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī, Durrat al-tāj (m: a target for acquisition, not yet evidence.
notes.Ibn Khaldūn, Muqaddima (the craft of sin: ʿaṣabiyya is a candidate measurable quantity for social cohesion, and Ibn Khaldūn gives it a life cycle (roughly three generations). It measures cohesion, not harmony.
notes.G. W. Leibniz, Monadology (pre-establish: and: the primary line I found is Mon. §58 (variety with order equals perfection). The formula "the highest perfection is the most complete unity or order in the greatest variety" is **Latta's editorial note 50**, not Leibniz. So prop-leibniz-product is verified only in this weaker form.

The formula "the highest perfection is the most complete unity or order in the greatest variety" is **Latta's editorial note 50**, not Leibniz. So prop-leibniz-product is verified only in this weaker form.
notes.Jean-Philippe Rameau, Treatise on Harmon: the Preface is a clear early *principle first, rules derived* programme, and he openly lets taste override it.
notes.Gustav Theodor Fechner, Introduction to: Fechner turns the principle into a judgment one can test. That is a historical precedent for measuring harmony before predicting with it.
notes.Cantares mexicanos (Nahua \"flower and s: Brinton's sources assign different songs to different months and moods (scan 20, not quoted here). Music matched to a calendar is a possible thing to measure, if the Nahuatl is read.
notes.Henri A. Junod, The Life of a South Afri: Junod asks for phonograph records of timbila players because they "play with two hands". That is a measure-first proposal, a century early.

ideas.q: Is understanding a kind of harmonising?

notes.Zhuangzi, \"Qiwulun\" and \"Xu Wugui\"||: "Great knowledge is wide and comprehensive; small knowledge is partial" (same book, p. 178). Harmonizing is a kind of seeing, not a kind of building.
notes.Jacob Boehme, The Signature of All Thing: "one property sees, tests, and wills another" is an old thesis that understanding needs a differentiated multiplicity.
notes.Popol Vuh|||Native American & Mesoameric: the gods keep failing and retrying ("Plus on y travaille...") until they get beings with speech and understanding. Creation is iterative design by a council.

ideas.q: Is agreement between parties a harmony, or a sameness?

notes.Ṛgveda|||Indian: X.191 is alignment as unanimity, "United be the thoughts of all". It is a useful ancient example of the alignment ideal that “Human–AI–nature alignment as harmony” has to distinguish itself from.
notes.Mataṅga, Bṛhaddeśī|||Indian: in the polity image, consonance is the minister's following (*anusāritva*) of the king. Here alignment means obedience to the dominant note.
notes.Analects 1.12 and 13.23 (he er bu tong)|: 13.23 gives a test for alignment between people. The small man agrees and is not in harmony. That is the same point as Yanzi's "assenter".
notes.Zuozhuan, Yanzi on harmony and sameness: Yanzi's minister is a model of alignment *by correction*. Agreeing is a failure of alignment, not its success. This is the strongest use of the passage.
notes.Zhuangzi, \"Qiwulun\" and \"Xu Wugui\"||: Zhuangzi's answer to conflicting views is not to align them. Both stay "admissible", and the sage stops trying to settle who is right. That is a real alternative to alignment-as-agreement, and a costly one: it gives up judgement.
notes.Xunzi, \"Discourse on Music\" (Yuelun)||: the clearest classical statement of alignment by *shared experience*. Ruler and minister listen to the same music and feel "harmony and reverence". It works, and it is explicitly a means of rule, so it is the risk the guard clause names.
notes.Lüshi chunqiu, the music chapters|||Chin: music is a ruler's instrument for unifying the state (以一治天下). See.
notes.Zhu Xi, on equilibrium and harmony (zhon: ritual without he is acceptable, but he without ritual is not. This is alignment to a fixed form as the precondition of harmony.
notes.Shōtoku Taishi, Seventeen-Article Consti: Articles 1 and 17 read as an alignment protocol. Discuss with many, reach one right conclusion, and then all comply. Agreement is the target, and standing disagreement counts as failure. That is the alignment-as-assimilation risk in its plainest form.
notes.Aristides Quintilianus, On Music|||Helle: and “Wellbeing, peace and sustainability as nested harmonizing”: "likeness or opposition" are two ways of bringing a disordered part into tune, by meeting it where it is or by pulling against it. The same choice appears in any alignment procedure.
notes.Nicole Oresme, On the Commensurability o: the gold:silver ratio is a proportion grounded in nature and kept out of the ruler's hands. This is a medieval case of a just measure that no single party may set.
notes.al-Ghazālī, the Book of Listening (samāʿ: "the same input, different effects depending on the receiver's state" is a usable analogy for alignment. Do not stretch it further.
notes.Rūmī, Masnavī (the song of the reed)|||P: the shepherd story is an argument against a single correct form of expression imposed by an authority (Moses). God judges the inward state, not conformity of speech.
notes.Marin Mersenne, Harmonie universelle|||R: **Cuts against.** He explicitly wants society to anneal toward unison (community of goods, "one same body and one same spirit"). He postpones it to a state of perfection, but he does not give it up.
notes.Popol Vuh|||Native American & Mesoameric: the gods want creatures aligned to them ("obéissants"; "who adore us and who invoke us", the library translation of scan 317). This is alignment as worship and service, and it is the risk the guard clause names.

ideas.q: Are health, peace and a lasting world kinds of harmony?
ideas.t: Wellbeing, peace and sustainability as nested harmonizing

notes.Bhagavad Gītā|||Indian: samatva is a serious wellbeing ideal. It is steadiness under gain and loss, close to the Stoic one. It belongs in idea 11 as *equanimity*. Labelling it "harmony" would hide that it works by detachment.
notes.Caraka Saṃhitā|||Indian: Āyurveda is a full-scale *balance* model of wellbeing. It has a diagnosis of imbalance, a therapy by opposites, and a norm of health as one's natural state. It belongs in idea 11 as homeostasis. It should be cited as such and not as diversity in wholeness.
notes.Vinaya, Mahāvagga V.1: Soṇa and the lute: it is a wellbeing teaching. Soṇa's bleeding feet are the cost of over-striving. "Even" effort is what lets the practice go on, and in the story it works: Soṇa becomes an arahat.
notes.Guoyu, Shi Bo in the \"Zhengyu\"|||Chine: 同則不繼 frames sameness as unsustainable, the nearest ancient analogue to the ecological diversity–stability claims. It is an analogy, not evidence.
notes.Zuozhuan, Yanzi on harmony and sameness: the Zichan story makes "harmony" in government compatible with lethal severity. That is a warning for any use of harmony as a peace word.
notes.Zhongyong (Doctrine of the Mean), ch. 1|: the claim that personal equilibrium nourishes "all things" is the classical form of wellbeing scaling up to the world. Legge calls the chapter "a mixture of sense and mysticism" (scan 358), so do not lean on it as argument.
notes.Lüshi chunqiu, the music chapters|||Chin: harmony as health. Fitting sound keeps the heart level and life long. Excessive music "harms life" (其生必傷).
notes.Liji, \"Record of Music\" (Yueji)|||Chin: and “Human–AI–nature alignment as harmony”: music is a tool by which "the minds of the people are assimilated". This is the explicit form of the risk that the guard clause names. The text gives alignment-as-assimilation in its own words.
notes.Shōtoku Taishi, Seventeen-Article Consti: the text does treat peace as a public good, and Article 16 limits forced labour to the season when farmers are idle. Concord here protects the people's livelihood, not only the court.
notes.Kangen ongi|||Japanese: music as medicine. "The Five Tones belong to the five organs", so harmony is health and discord is illness.
notes.Kaibara Ekiken, on music and harmony|||J: music as medicine. "The Five Tones belong to the five organs", so harmony is health and discord is illness.
notes.Plato, Phaedo (the soul as attunement)||: harmony within (soul), between (city, chorus) and with the whole (learning the cosmos's harmonies, Timaeus 90d) appear as one programme, already in Plato.
notes.Plato, Republic (the harmonised soul and: harmony within (soul), between (city, chorus) and with the whole (learning the cosmos's harmonies, Timaeus 90d) appear as one programme, already in Plato.
notes.Plato, Timaeus|||Greek: harmony within (soul), between (city, chorus) and with the whole (learning the cosmos's harmonies, Timaeus 90d) appear as one programme, already in Plato.
notes.Plato, Philebus|||Greek: harmony within (soul), between (city, chorus) and with the whole (learning the cosmos's harmonies, Timaeus 90d) appear as one programme, already in Plato.
notes.Theon of Smyrna, Mathematics Useful for: "to make enemies into friends … through the art of music or the art of medicine" puts peace and health under one craft.
notes.Plotinus, Enneads (IV.4 on sympathy)|||H: harmony within (III.6, the parts of the soul) and with the whole (III.2, IV.4) form one scheme, but Plotinus gives no account of harmony *between* persons.
notes.Boethius, On the Institution of Music|||: and the guard clause: I.1 (after Plato) says that changing a people's music corrupts its morals. Together with I.34's master/slave ranking of reason over hand, harmony here licenses the regulation of taste. applies.
notes.Boethius, Consolation of Philosophy II m: and the guard clause: I.1 (after Plato) says that changing a people's music corrupts its morals. Together with I.34's master/slave ranking of reason over hand, harmony here licenses the regulation of taste. applies.
notes.Augustine, On Music|||Early Christian &: Caution for “Wellbeing, peace and sustainability as nested harmonizing”: XI.18 is a theodicy. "Every evil serves the whole" can justify any harm, which is the misuse that names.
notes.Augustine, City of God XI.18|||Early Chr: Caution for “Wellbeing, peace and sustainability as nested harmonizing”: XI.18 is a theodicy. "Every evil serves the whole" can justify any harm, which is the misuse that names.
notes.Hildegard of Bingen, Scivias and Ordo Vi: song as a therapy of the soul (point 1), set beside a medicine of humoral balance (point 5). This is a 12th-century case of harmony used for wellbeing.
notes.Nicholas of Cusa, The Catholic Concordan: *De pace fidei* (1453), written after the fall of Constantinople, is a peace plan. Its premise is that people kill one another over the diversity of rites.
notes.al-Fārābī, Great Book of Music|||Arabic: mutual assistance is directed toward happiness, and he warns that a city can also cooperate toward bad ends.
notes.al-Fārābī, The Virtuous City|||Arabic: mutual assistance is directed toward happiness, and he warns that a city can also cooperate toward bad ends.
notes.Ikhwān al-Ṣafāʾ, Epistle on Music|||Arab: music in hospitals and temples is a historical case of harmony used for wellbeing, with an explicit warning that the same means can be misused.
notes.Pico della Mirandola, 900 Theses and Hep: music as medicine acting through the soul (point 4).
notes.Francesco Giorgi, On the Harmony of the: the Tabernacle that is taken down and put up again (point 4) is an image of wholeness *in time*: the whole persists while its parts are dissolved and recomposed.
notes.Paracelsus, Great Astronomy (Astronomia: the "league of twenty men" image (point 3) is his own bridge from the body to a political body.
notes.Guillaume Postel, On the Concord of the: an early-modern programme for world peace through religion: one law, one peace, conversion "without sedition", and a ban on cursing between confessions (1551). Its peace requires a single persuasion. Aristotle's warning against making "a harmony into a unison" is the classical objection.

notes.Athanasius Kircher, Musurgia universalis: tarantism is harmony used as therapy. The fatal double bite is an image of fragmentation: opposites with no resolution.
notes.Comenius, The Way of Light|||Renaissance: the most developed early-modern programme for peace through education and shared knowledge. Use it with point 3's caution.
notes.Shaftesbury, Characteristics|||Renaissan: health of body and of mind fall under one proportion-concept.
notes.Cantares mexicanos (Nahua \"flower and s: "peace, and goodfellowship... let all join hands" ties peace to shared dance, under the shadow of death. It is festival conviviality, not a political doctrine.
notes.Washington Matthews, The Mountain Chant: the strongest fit. Hózhó joins health, beauty, long life, rain, corn and the kin group in one word. That is a wellbeing concept across levels, from the body to the land.
notes.N. B. Emerson, Unwritten Literature of H: *pono* "for us both" makes wellbeing a property of a relationship, not of one person. That is a useful formulation for idea 11.

stories.title: Huygens's two clocks
stories.line: Two pendulum clocks on one beam fall into step and stay there. Huygens first calls it "a kind of sympathy", then finds the cause in the beam: sympathy becomes synchronisation.

stories.title: The music of the spheres
stories.line: The planets sound as they move, at intervals that make a scale, and we do not hear it. Denied by Aristotle, kept by the Platonists, turned by Kepler into the ratios of the planets' speeds.

verdict.title: Is harmony found in every tradition?
verdict.text: Words for fit, measure, balance and concord turn up in every tradition on this map. Whether they mean what most of these sources mean by harmony, unlike parts held together in one whole with each kept different, is another matter. Where a reader checked a source’s own word against that sense, it matched in 2 of 44 cases, in part in 22, and not at all in 20. In the Navajo, Nahua, Kʼicheʼ, Thonga, Māori and Hawaiian sources the library holds, the editors who recorded them translated no word as "harmony": the nearest words mean beauty and long life, rightness, or joining.
